correctness.rationale: For each node the neighbor sum is bounded by its degree; if j>Delta its opposing-pair inhibitory contribution strictly determines the sign. The full map is F(A,B)=(-B,-A) without ties and F squared is the identity. All-positive configurations show this exact map fails below degree maximum, and tie randomness shows failure at equality. Fixed-point equation A=-B gives 2^N; every other orbit has two distinct elements. The exact independent product law gives Binomial(N,2r(1-r)) flipping sites, stationary probability [r^2+(1-r)^2]^N and both homogeneous polarized probabilities r^(2N)+(1-r)^(2N). The standalone exact verifier exhausts graph/state pairs only up to N=3; the unrestricted proof is the sign inequality and counting.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 opinion-dynamics work interprets antagonism through polarization/metastability and two particular absorbing consensus states. A motivated unresolved boundary is what occurs if one-to-one inhibition becomes stronger than all same-layer social influence. The exact sharp degree barrier reveals a global dynamical regime with exponentially many genuine two-cycles, 2^N distinct frozen microstates, graph-independent orbit structure and a binomial prediction under exactly the published initialization law. For any interior initial bias, almost every large-N state cycles rather than converges. This is a complete natural phase classification, not a routine strengthening of an arbitrary numeric sample; it supplies a mathematically necessary caveat to extrapolating polarized selection across arbitrary inhibitory strengths. No downstream theorem beyond this exact structure is claimed.
